title: Famous problems, network coding and quantum computing
made_with: AI agents (Claude) directed by the author; usually one AI skeptic per result, a few had two or three, some none; nothing found in these rounds is checked in Lean (preprints-8 is a cross-reference to a Lean-proved result of another section); no person has read the arguments
guard: no claim of the author's own about any network-coding conjecture, and nothing about the correctness of the two network-coding preprints of 7 October 2026

findings.statement: The problem is not another famous problem in disguise: it is the classic question whether the Fourier transform's N log N can be beaten, answered yes by OpenAI's preprints of September 2026; the refined question, the exact value of the best saving, has no famous name that the surveys found.
findings.status_detail: a literature reading by five survey agents, each read by one AI skeptic, plus a completeness critic; no person has checked it

findings.statement: The best DFT saving (all lengths) equals the best saving for exact complex polynomial multiplication (cyclic convolution): convolution theorem one way, Bluestein's trick with linearisation (at most 3x) the other.
findings.status_detail: a standard argument; the identities checked by computer for n = 1 to 40 by an AI skeptic

findings.statement: The best WHT saving equals the XOR-convolution saving and the saving of the Kronecker powers of every invertible 2x2 kernel that is not a permutation times a diagonal (Yates's zeta transform, the disjointness matrix, OpenAI's kernel C), via (-1)^(x.y) = i^|x| i^|y| i^(-|x xor y|) and H = U diag(1,-2) P U P.
findings.status_detail: the identity checked exactly by computer up to N = 128 and over finite fields, by two agents independently; one AI skeptic upheld the relation

findings.statement: Proving that the best saving is below 1 would give a superlinear lower bound for an explicit linear map (Valiant's problem) and, through WHT(n^2) <= 6 MM(n), a lower bound of about n^2 (log n)^eps for matrix multiplication; the links run one way and the two consequences are nested.
findings.status_detail: the AI skeptics of three surveys upheld the link to Valiant's problem and two upheld the link to matrix multiplication; one built Strassen's algorithm as a circuit (n = 2, 4), fixed one factor to H and linearised it exactly within 6 C(n) gates; s* < 1 gives a bound only infinitely often

findings.statement: The construction side and the restricted-game bounds match no famous open problem: each open unit question (fixed W, M, m, game and scratch bound) is a finite system of polynomial equations, decidable over C; hard by size, not by depth.
findings.status_detail: argued in the survey; no skeptic disputed it

findings.statement: The saving for H equals the saving for the single quadratic polynomial y^T H x within a factor 15 (Baur-Strassen reverse mode, then linearisation).
findings.status_detail: no AI skeptic has read it; one exact test on H with up to 32 points and on random matrices (constant 12 on those instances)

findings.statement: Classical simulation of a Hadamard layer or the QFT on a state vector is literally the WHT or the DFT; the units are the first such simulations whose saving grows with n (not the first below n 2^n: Alman and Rao's 23/24 and the 5/6 result came first); at 40 qubits a saving of 1.63e-3 is worth a factor of about 1.006.
findings.status_detail: a literal restatement; one AI skeptic upheld it and corrected the 'first below n 2^n' wording

findings.statement: The best DFT saving and the best WHT saving are two numbers not known to be equal; OpenAI's DFT preprint carries unit-type Kronecker constructions to the DFT at every length, but no reduction is known for arbitrary circuits or from the DFT to the WHT.
findings.status_detail: an AI skeptic's correction of an earlier summary that treated them as one number; a later argument (16 October, idea-rounds section) via Rader's trick over finite fields is not checked

findings.statement: The network coding conjecture (Li and Li; Harvey, Kleinberg and Lehman) implies a best saving of 0, through the shift-network map of Afshani, Freksen, Kamma and Larsen; the networks this map makes from a saving of 1.68e-3 need log2 N of at least 2^595 (about 2^1786 with the guaranteed constant loss of about 8). No claim is made about the conjecture itself.
findings.status_detail: the implication is the published map, re-derived step by step by one agent; an AI skeptic checked its finite-field step by computer and corrected the constant from about 2 to about 8

findings.statement: Rigidity, Strassen's asymptotic spectrum, direct-sum problems, Alman's bounded-depth results, Morgenstern's and Ailon's restricted models, quantum gate counts, stabiliser rank, index coding and the group FFT conjecture have the same shape as the problem or share tools with it; none is a reduction. The Hadamard conjecture, orthogonal designs, the asymptotic rank conjecture, Cohn-Umans, VP vs VNP, P vs NP, log-rank, sunflower, Kakeya and Hilbert's 10th and 13th problems have no relation.
findings.status_detail: one AI skeptic per area corrected the relation types (rigidity upgraded to shared tools; direct sum downgraded to an analogy; Sylvester-Gallai, design matrices and cap sets downgraded to none or tools)

findings.statement: The community's 120 E8 labels and the 135 block-3 frames are the nonsingular and singular points of one quadric O+(8,2), with explicit isomorphisms; E8's packing and kissing properties play no part.
findings.status_detail: an AI skeptic computed the isomorphisms with its own code

findings.statement: For relabellings that form a 2-group, the frustration classes of two-array separations are exactly the nonzero cosets of RM(1,k), also with X letters allowed; an order-3 letter breaks the picture (two pieces suffice).
findings.status_detail: checked by computer on small cases; one AI skeptic

findings.statement: Whether a better complex unit says anything about OpenAI's integer-multiplication exponent is unresolved: the skeptics label the relation shared tools or same shape, the critic one-way.
findings.status_detail: the labels disagree

findings.statement: The transform game's complex side has an exact stabiliser dictionary: frames are Lagrangians (stabiliser states up to sign), free steps on one array are the Hadamard-free Clifford group up to scalars, a paid move is sqrt(X) after a CNOT circuit (one Hadamard up to free gates and e^(i pi/4)), frame distance is the least Hadamard count of the transition Clifford, subspace frames are S-twisted CSS states, the frame graph is the dual polar graph of Sp(2m,2), and the E8 knows-pattern is the commutation graph of the 120 odd-Y four-qubit Paulis.
findings.status_detail: every row computed exactly at small m (m <= 3 or 4) by one agent and recomputed by an AI skeptic with its own code written from the Lean engine's definitions

findings.statement: The stabiliser link 'appears new as a connection'.
findings.status_detail: every fact is textbook quantum information, and the Clifford reading of frames was already in the community (icekylinx's general Clifford frame lemma, pull request #130; eumemic's pull request #288; the community's exact-Clifford scripts and Lean file) and in this project's notes of 9 October
findings.refuted_by: the novelty skeptic of the quantum round, 13 October

findings.statement: Interval lemma: the frames on shortest paths between two frames at distance d are exactly those Z with Z = (Z cap X) + (Z cap Y) and form a copy of the subspace lattice of F_2^d; so shortest paths from start to end pass only through subspace frames (in quantum words, a stabiliser group lies on a shortest path from |0..0> to |+..+> exactly when it is CSS).
findings.status_detail: two AI skeptics re-derived it; checked by computer on every pair at m = 2, 3 and 94,095 pairs at m = 4; its use for the copy wall assumes ports run without detours

findings.statement: Labels on non-subspace frames (avenue 4) are dead in their simple form: the start frame's 2(2^h - 1) neighbours split half and half, subspace neighbours h - 1 moves from the end and the others h moves, so a non-subspace label costs h + 1 instead of h.
findings.status_detail: checked by computer for m <= 4 and h <= 9 (511 + 511 at h = 9); one AI skeptic

findings.statement: In the engine's wider game a target can cancel a source it does not know, using fixed twists between terms in one array (labels 001 and 111 share one total at copy cost 2 at m = 3); the twisted relation is exactly twice the orthogonal one at odd sizes (12 vs 6 at m = 3; 65,280 vs 32,640 at h = 9) and less at even sizes (56 vs 32 at m = 4); it is unrelated to non-subspace frames and not legal in the community's format.
findings.status_detail: exhaustive over all 720 and 1,451,520 symplectic twists at m = 2, 3; both AI skeptics rebuilt the example with their own code and corrected 'exactly doubles'

findings.statement: A pair saves nothing: a total's copy cost is at least the F_2-rank of a twisted cross-Gram matrix with unit diagonal, so a total whose interference is cancelled directly costs at least one move per port; for a pair that is 2, the cost of two separate totals.
findings.status_detail: two AI skeptics; one extended the bound to totals that walk through several frames

findings.statement: 'With timing respected, even the old rule cannot share one total.'
findings.status_detail: true only for the searched shape: a longer walk shares one total at copy cost 3, worse than 2
findings.refuted_by: a sandwich skeptic's explicit schedule at m = 2

findings.statement: On the community's E8 frame decoder with a different twist per total, a SAT encoding of a generous relaxation makes copy cost 63 unsatisfiable and reaches 64 with the community's labels; one twist for the whole family lowers no total from 8 to 7; small families (h = 3, 4; every 4-port pattern with payload F_3 or F_5) cost one copy move per port.
findings.status_detail: one program each, not repeated by anyone; the SAT encoding has not been re-checked; in a looser encoding (one modelling condition dropped) 62 becomes satisfiable, so the result rests on that condition

findings.statement: With payload F_2 the copy cost is at least one move per port for every label family and every twist.
findings.status_detail: a short proof; no AI skeptic has read it

findings.statement: What-if prices with this project's copy of the community's pricing program (control: the community's record 1.6644e-3 to the last digit): one copy move fewer per call gives 1.7112e-3 (+2.81 %); one whole total fewer per call gives 2.0385e-3 (+22.47 %, bit side then binding at 1.7304e-3). Neither construction exists.
findings.status_detail: a price computed by a program for constructions that do not exist (what-if), not a result

findings.statement: Frames are described exactly by a subspace U and a symmetric form beta (Dehaene-De Moor); the excess of a frame (extra moves any path through it pays) has histogram {0: 16, 1: 35, 2: 56, 3: 28} at m = 3, and excess = rank(beta - dot) for m <= 4.
findings.status_detail: the histogram confirmed by two independent recounts; the rank formula checked by one program for m <= 4, not repeated

findings.statement: Bravyi-Maslov normal form in the engine's matrices: a run of letters on one array equals free * one block of rank r * free, so a search needs at most one block per array between additions that touch it.
findings.status_detail: computed at m <= 2 in the engine's own matrices; not repeated by anyone

findings.statement: At m = 1 all 96 group elements stay linearly independent once up to 6 digit columns are tested, so the every-f rule makes cancellation exact there; at f = 1 the kernel would be a free combination, which is why single-copy quantum identities do not transfer.
findings.status_detail: one program, not repeated by anyone; larger m untested

findings.statement: The distance between subspace frames is the Koetter-Kschischang subspace distance of random network coding, and the frame distance extends it; the copy floor is a linear index-coding (minrank) problem whose side-information graph at E8 is the commutation graph of the 120 odd-Y four-qubit Paulis, of which the largest pairwise anticommuting set has 8 members (so the minrank is at least 8 over every field).
findings.status_detail: computed for m <= 4 (distance) and exhaustively (the 120 Paulis); one program for the anticommuting bound

findings.statement: A common-frame (coherent) unit is a vector-linear network code over C on the frame graph, one session per array between opposite frames; a saver is a code that beats routing (m moves per input). The reading is first in the community's pull request #288.
findings.status_detail: several AI readings in October found no gap; no person has checked it

findings.statement: Lemma 1: the uniform layout (every ordered opposite pair equally often) is the worst for common-frame units, because Sp(2m,2) is transitive on ordered opposite pairs; one number per block caps every common-frame unit.
findings.status_detail: the AI skeptic checked the symmetry facts by computer (transitive on 120 and 8,640 ordered opposite pairs and on arcs at blocks 2, 3)

findings.statement: On the uniform layout the cut bound is 1.5, 1.75 and 1.875 moves per array at blocks 2, 3, 4 (saving ceilings 0.415, 0.491, 0.547 for common-frame units), against certificates 2, 2.8, 41/13 (ceilings 0, 0.0628, 0.1714).
findings.status_detail: the cut constants recomputed by two AI skeptics

findings.statement: Lemma 3: any entropy LP that writes its network rows for only some node sets is capped by plain routing on the lumped network, whatever valid inequalities for linear codes it adds (Shannon, Ingleton, DFZ); Lemma 4: lumping into four groups or fewer never beats the cut bound. So no entropy LP small enough to solve proves more than the cut bound on Gamma_2, Gamma_3, Gamma_4.
findings.status_detail: the AI skeptic reproduced the values but wrote no separate check of these two proofs

findings.statement: Lumping searches: at block 2 the smallest lumping that beats cuts has five groups (rho = 1.6, a K_{2,3}) and 26 LP variables; reaching the certificate needs all 15 frames apart; at block 3 no lumping below 14 groups beat 1.75 and about 124 of 135 frames must stay apart for 2.8; at block 4 lumpings up to 300 groups stay below 1.875 and about 2,027 of 2,295 frames must stay apart for 41/13 (2,026 cells still fall short).
findings.status_detail: exact for the lumpings found; that no smaller lumping does better is a search result, not a proof

findings.statement: Calibration: the entropy LP gives 8 on the Okamura-Seymour network (cuts 6, routing 8; rigorous bound 7.9999986) and no coding gain for any rates there, finds the butterfly's gain 8/7, but gives only 70.8 against routing 80 on K_{2,3} with two-way sessions; the skeptic's own LP finds the combination network's gain (9 vs 10) and reproduces the three-group lumping of Gamma_2 (80); the Ingleton and DFZ rows are encoded correctly.
findings.status_detail: one AI skeptic repeated parts with its own code

findings.statement: Lemma W (two-class stretch): if the pairs of a layout split into two stretchable sets, every common-frame unit with that layout needs W*m moves, at every block and every W.
findings.status_detail: one AI skeptic re-derived it and checked its packings exactly on 300 random layouts for each W = 3..6 at each block 2..4

findings.statement: Lemma W+: a three-pair layout with cross deficiency e needs at least 3m - e moves for a common-frame unit; e <= 1 for about 99.45 % of random layouts at block 4, so a common-frame 3 in 10 at block 4 is excluded on all of them.
findings.status_detail: one AI skeptic re-derived it and checked the near-polygon fact by brute force (all 840 and 613,440 triples at blocks 2, 3; 381,300 at block 4)

findings.statement: Every three-pair layout at block 4 that anyone solved on all of Gamma_4 (37, most hill-climbed toward the worst case) has cut value exactly 12; of 709 random three-pair layouts, 531 are covered by Lemma W and the other 178 certified by the exact screen or the full LP.
findings.status_detail: the AI skeptic repeated values with its own LPs and solved the 16 hard layouts the author had left; the author's full solves use the directed LP (sampled orientation), the skeptic's undirected solves cover every orientation

findings.statement: Cut gaps exist with four or more arrays: at block 3 a triangle-plus-pendant layout has cut value 11 against 12; at block 4 two such layouts have 14 and 15 against 16, so cuts cannot exclude a common-frame 4 in 14 or 4 in 15 at block 4; at block 3 with five arrays layouts reach 14 and 13, so cuts cannot exclude 5 in 14 there; at block 2 cut values fall short from five arrays on although Theorem 2W makes routing optimal.
findings.status_detail: one AI skeptic (the block-4 four-array gaps are the skeptic's)
supersedes: 'cut gaps at W = 4 show cuts cannot settle 4 in 13 to 4 in 15' (block 4)

findings.statement: Zhang, Li and Li's code (arXiv:2610.09367) cannot become a saving unit: its coefficients are integers and it never divides, while every unit the engine accepts that saves must divide by 2 in a free step.
findings.status_detail: rests on an in-house argument read only by AI agents (statement B of the fourth revision's network-coding note); one AI skeptic gave this shorter form; nothing is claimed about the preprint's correctness

findings.statement: Braverman and He's code (arXiv:2610.10108) gets its gain from the field with 9 elements: a rebuild from its published lists gives 166 free symbols there (131 without the cubing at lines), while the same integer rule read in Z[i]/p for p = 10007 and 1000003 keeps only 25, where a gain needs at least 152; no rational code with these sessions is known.
findings.status_detail: one program, re-run for this revision with the same output; the AI skeptic did not repeat the rank computations; nothing is claimed about the preprint's correctness

findings.statement: The Braverman-He graph cannot be laid on the block-5 frame graph with every edge one move and every session's ends 5 apart: 1,524 forced cases need 8 or 9 different first steps between vertices 3 apart, where every frame graph has exactly 7.
findings.status_detail: argued by hand with a computer count: the step from 5-edge routes to shortest paths is an argument; the 7 first steps are computed at blocks 3 and 4 and recalled as a standard fact at block 5; the 1,524 forced cases are counted by computer. The AI skeptic reproduced the count with separate loops and found the argument sound for block 5 with every edge one move

findings.statement: Blocks 3 and 4 are excluded for the Braverman-He code because 735 moves exceed 157*4 and 157*3.
findings.status_detail: two vertices placed on one frame exchange symbols for free, so collapsed edges lower the count

findings.statement: At block 4 the Braverman-He code gives no saving under any placement: collapsed edges form a matching (at most 91), leaving at least 644 moves against 628.
findings.status_detail: the AI skeptic's argument with a computer count; no second skeptic

findings.statement: With 157 arrays at block 5 and 735 rank-1 moves, a translated unit would save 4.09e-2 (4.23e-2 by the whole-block bound); 0.1 would need 14.9 % saved and more than 19.0 % of the edges free, against the preprint's 17.6 % and 18.2 %. Not a ceiling over all placements.
findings.status_detail: a price computed by a program for a construction that does not exist

findings.statement: The engine's phase letter makes Gaussian coefficients available to a translated code.
findings.status_detail: the letter multiplies an array by i^f, not by i, so a unit must be right with i replaced by 1 and -1; the lift a code needs is to the rationals
findings.refuted_by: the preprint-reading skeptic, reading the Lean letter definitions

findings.statement: The open case of the fourth revision's network-coding note (three messages at block 3 in the operator model, which is the engine game: 8 or 9 paid moves?) is closed: 9 are needed, by the block-3 bound 14W/5 = 8.4 for W = 3.
findings.status_detail: a corollary of the block-3 bound 14W/5, proved in Lean in the engine game with only the three standard axioms (14 October); recorded here as a cross-reference because it closes a case this repository listed as open; the proof belongs to the block-bounds-and-new-rules section
supersedes: 'W = 3 in 8 moves at block 3 is open' (fourth revision, notes/for-network-coding-readers.md, section 3)

findings.statement: The units are the first exact Hadamard-layer simulations below n 2^n operations.
findings.status_detail: Alman and Rao's 23/24 and the 5/6 result came first; the units are the first whose saving grows with n

findings.statement: With one array the game is a solved quantum problem.
findings.status_detail: only with no scratch arrays and no mixing, which is not one of the games; with mixing, one array needs m moves by a count of nonzeros along paths

findings.statement: The shift networks are about 2 times below the plain FFT in general.
findings.status_detail: that holds on the plain FFT's own graph; the guarantee for any degree-3 network is about 8

findings.statement: A paid move is one Hadamard gate.
findings.status_detail: as a cost yes, up to free gates and a scalar; the gate itself is sqrt(X)

note_on_counts: preprints-8 is a cross-reference to a result of the block-bounds-and-new-rules section; an index that sums sections should not count it twice

open.question: Does every three-pair layout on Gamma_4 have cut value above 11 (so every common-frame unit with at most three arrays needs W*m)?
open.first_experiment: Lemma W proves cut value above 11 only for e = 0; for e = 1 Lemma W+ gives 11, which excludes 3 in 10 but not 3 in 11. Exhaustive solving is out of reach (at least about 5.7e6 symmetry classes of three-pair layouts, 4.6e7 if each pair's direction counts, and about 1.5e6 with e >= 1, at 20-60 minutes of LP each). Take the LP duals of the 37 solved layouts, see which cut families they use (w3probe.py), and look for one family (like the level sets behind Lemma W+) giving at least 3m - 0.5 on every layout with e >= 1; test on the hill-climbed layouts before proving.

open.question: Can cuts exclude a common-frame 4 in 13 at block 4?
open.first_experiment: layout_search.py at block 4, W = 4, seeded with triangle-plus-pendant layouts, looking for cut value <= 13.

open.question: How strong is a non-lumped (partial polymatroid) entropy LP on Gamma_m?
open.first_experiment: At block 2, variables only for the arc sets at one frame together with the sessions starting or ending there; solve and compare with the cut bound 1.5.

open.question: Is the E8 twisted-decoder SAT result (63 impossible) right, and do decoders other than the frame decoder do better with a twist per total?
open.first_experiment: A skeptic re-encodes the model from its definition and re-runs 'min 7'; then extend the label-decoder SAT with twist groups.

open.question: Can a detour through a non-subspace frame shared by several ports pay for itself?
open.first_experiment: Extend twist.py's exhaustive search at m = 3 to totals with one detour step, on families of three and four ports.

open.question: What is the minrank of the commutation graph of the 120 odd-Y four-qubit Paulis over F_2, F_3 and Q?
open.first_experiment: Lovasz theta and Haemers-type bounds of the 120-vertex graph (seconds), then a SAT search for low-rank fitting matrices over F_2 and F_3.

open.question: Is there a rational code of Braverman-He type (local rules with far more solutions than counting allows) on the block-3 frame graph?
open.first_experiment: Local rules invariant under two or three subgroups of the block-3 symmetry group; solution dimension by a rank computation; stop if no rule keeps more than a third of the edges free. Odds under 2 %.

open.question: Is the factor-15 equivalence between H and y^T H x right?
open.first_experiment: A skeptic re-derives it and extends k1_baur_strassen.py to random straight-line circuits for q with cancelling junk.

open.question: Does a better complex unit say anything about OpenAI's integer-multiplication exponent?
open.first_experiment: Write out which of the two capping procedures a complex unit would replace, with the preprint's parameters.

open.question: Do the units give o(N log N) synchronous circuits in Alman's model?
open.first_experiment: Count the wires of one recursion level of the smallest published unit with the scratch arrays laid out as that model requires.

open.question: Is a saving of 1.68e-3 above the coding-gap exponents that follow from the two preprints' constructions?
open.first_experiment: Compute the missing amplification parameter from the published amplification theorem (a comparison of exponents, not a check of either preprint).

open.question: What does the WHT result give for subset convolution over C, against the literature?
open.first_experiment: A literature search for the best known operation count of subset convolution over C.

open.question: Could a block-3 placement of the Braverman-He sessions collapse at least 265 edges (313 for 0.1)?
open.first_experiment: Only meaningful once a rational code exists (open-7); then a SAT search for placements with many collapsed edges using skeptic_collapsed_edges.py's forced pairs.
